title: Red ink, fresh capital all around
deck: English football's clubs booked a record pre-tax loss even as private capital pushed deeper into the game around them — buying the agencies, the media-rights arms, and rewriting who is even allowed to own a club.

title: Who sets the terms
deck: A week when the money kept pushing into football but its members, ownership rules and financial regulators kept deciding the terms — FIFA's World Cup sale collapsed, a Liverpool investor had to give up another club, and Saudi Arabia bought out the dealmaker behind its Newcastle takeover.

title: Selling the slice
deck: A $6bn price tag on Liverpool, leagues cashing in their TV rights, and a debt-built empire unravelling in court — a week when football kept selling pieces of itself without letting go.

title: Changing hands
deck: The week football spent less time on the scoreboard than on the plumbing behind it — who sells its rights, who finances its stadiums, and where the World Cup's record billions landed.

title: The great repricing
deck: World Cup rights, shirt fronts, and slices of its biggest clubs — even as the tournament itself broke every commercial record it had.

title: The rules switch on
deck: England's regulator went live, the leveraged multi-club model kept unwinding, and capital kept buying football's rights and cashflows rather than its clubs.

title: Demand meets distress
deck: Tottenham's stake sale, Botafogo's bankruptcy, football's crowded private-equity field, PIF's stadium financing, FIFA's late World Cup rights, and the commercial money finding new doors.

title: The Phase 2 reset
deck: PIF's strategy reset, Apollo's Atlético operating reset, Gamma Waves Partners, Two Circles' footprint, and the Independent Football Regulator's first year.
